body:
For #404 I parsed the config file rather than calling kubectl for performance reasons since kubectl is significantly slower than parsing the config (see benchmark below). I think it should be possible to simply split the env var and iterate over the files looking for the config but we probably need to double check how the merging take place. 

```
❯ hyperfine --warmup 5 "target/release/starship module kubernetes" "kubectl config view --minify --output \"jsonpath={.current-context}/{..namespace}\""
Benchmark #1: target/release/starship module kubernetes
  Time (mean ± σ):       5.0 ms ±   1.6 ms    [User: 1.8 ms, System: 1.9 ms]
  Range (min … max):     3.5 ms …  14.3 ms    387 runs
 
  Warning: Command took less than 5 ms to complete. Results might be inaccurate.
  Warning: Statistical outliers were detected. Consider re-running this benchmark on a quiet PC without any interferences from other programs. It might help to use the '--warmup' or '--prepare' options.
 
Benchmark #2: kubectl config view --minify --output "jsonpath={.current-context}/{..namespace}"
  Time (mean ± σ):     183.2 ms ±   7.0 ms    [User: 174.8 ms, System: 19.7 ms]
  Range (min … max):   174.2 ms … 194.2 ms    15 runs
 
Summary
  'target/release/starship module kubernetes' ran
   36.89 ± 11.99 times faster than 'kubectl config view --minify --output "jsonpath={.current-context}/{..namespace}"'
```

@andytom could you try getting the kubectl config via `kubectl config view --raw` instead of reading it from file? The advantage is that this command will return the full config, even if it's comprised of multiple files, and then you can just process it as before. 
I haven't benchmarked it but it seems pretty fast.
